item.title: Supporting App for Oracle SBC CDR - v1.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
* CRITICAL: disconnect\_cause was declared twice in the Stop record field list, at positions 17 and 134. Splunk took the first, so for three releases the field held Oracle's coarse outcome category and the Q.850 cause at position 134 had no field name at all and could not be searched. Position 17 is now cisco\_disconnect\_cause, which is Oracle's own name for it, and disconnect\_cause now holds the Q.850 cause. If you have saved searches or dashboards matching on disconnect\_cause values, they are matching the coarse category and need to move to cisco\_disconnect\_cause. * CRITICAL: calling\_mos, called\_mos, calling\_r\_factor and called\_r\_factor now hold the actual score. Oracle writes all four multiplied by 100 so that an integer attribute can carry a fraction - a MOS of 4.3 arrives on the wire as 430 - and the fields previously passed that through, so any threshold written against them was wrong by two orders of magnitude. The wire value is still available as calling\_mos\_raw and so on. A zero in these columns means the SBC has no QoS feature set enabled rather than a call scoring 0.0, so zero now reads as null. * The app now extracts a ciscoguid from accounting\_call\_id, so SBC records can be rolled up with CUCM, CUBE and CVP data where the deployment carries the identifier across. * Added worst\_mos and worst\_r\_factor, the score of the worse of the two directions. For some statistical analysis end-users will want to exclude the "not bad" side. These new fields will now let them do that more easily. * Oracle SBC CDR's two disconnect cause spaces are finally extracted as separate fields. Added q850\_cause\_description and cisco\_cause\_description, which describe the two cause spaces separately, from a new cause\_descriptions lookup. * the now-general "cause\_description" values now list the most specific reason available: the Q.850 cause where there is a meaningful one, and Oracle's coarse category where there is not. Prior to this release, cause\_description was simply giving the RADIUS accounting termination cause (still available as accounting\_termination\_cause\_description). * Added a ciscoguid\_family field, which reports whether a ciscoguid is an H.225-format guid or a time-based UUID. This was previously only available via a search macro that misreported any record carrying two guids. * The descriptions shown for SIP response codes, ie the sip\_status\_description field, have been rewritten from the IETF specifications that define each code - RFC 3261, plus the fifteen later RFCs that define the codes RFC 3261 does not cover. The codes themselves and their reason phrases (sip\_status\_code and sip\_status\_name) are unchanged. If you have saved searches, alerts or dashboards that match on the old description text rather than on sip\_status\_code, update them. * Added a health check that lists any saved search, dashboard or macro still using the old west/east media flow field names, with the name that replaces each. Run it as a user with admin\_all\_objects for a complete inventory. * Added a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md file to the app, itemizing the third-party components it bundles and the origin of the data in each of its reference lookups.


Description:
This app provides the Splunk configuration to ingest the CDR data from Oracle SBC. It is intended to work for both Oracle Session Router CDR and Oracle SBC CDR, although some unknowns remain as of this writing. It is also designed to work as a Supporting App alongside Sideview's commercial "Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics" app. When used in conjunction with the Cisco CDR app, the Oracle SBC data can be used in that app alongside the CUCM data.

item.title: Supporting Add-on for Oracle SBC CDR - v1.0.2 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
* Fixed the party number extractions on records whose SIP display name contains a comma, as "Last, First" from a corporate directory does. The station id fields are quoted for that reason, but the extraction walked the line by commas without honouring the quoting, so such a record was read one field out of step: callingPartyNumber came out empty and calledPartyNumber held the CALLING party's number, while the real called number was lost. * These are index-time fields, so the correction applies to newly indexed data only. Events already in the index keep the shifted values.


Description:
This app provides the index-time configuration to ingest the CDR data from Oracle Session Border Controller (Oracle SBC) and also from Oracle Session Router. Specifically the CSV-formatted CDR format that you get if you enable local cdr storage on the oracle boxes. The app correctly separates the intermingled start, interim and end records of this dataset, into three distinct sourcetypes, and extract the fields from each correctly. Note that although you can use it purely to onboard the data, this app contains NO search-time config and will not by itself extract the search-time fields properly. This is because it is designed to always work in conjunction with Sideview's "Supporting App for Oracle SBC", which is to be installed on the Search Head and which handles the search-time field extractions among other things. Furthermore ,both of these apps together are also designed to work with Sideview's "Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics" app. When all three pieces are used together, the solution gives users a more general Investigation and Reporting solution for Oracle SBC and Oracle Session Router. The use cases are actually nearly endless so please contact Sideview if you have questions or would just like to find out more. this app is a part of Sideview's overall Investigation and Reporting solution, and you can find more documentation on the Sideview website: https://sideviewapps.com/documentation/oracle-sbc-cdr

item.title: Supply Chain and AI Threat Intelligence Platform - v1.2.17 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

SCIP v1.2.17 — MITRE ATLAS coverage expansion, severity re-rating, compliance citation corrections, and audit fixes

This release consolidates the work in v1.2.15, v1.2.16 and v1.2.17 since the last published release (v1.2.14). The AI/agentic detection library grows from 66 to 81 rules (72 MITRE ATLAS-mapped, 9 vendor-defined). No cryptographic surface was modified.

New detections (15)

Fifteen new AI and agentic threat detections were added, covering: an AI service API used as a covert command-and-control channel; AI supply-chain rug pulls, where an established component's newly published content turns malicious; artifact repositories used as dead-drop C2 channels; agent runtime capability discovery; and sub-technique coverage for dataset and capability acquisition, autonomous exploit and agent tool development, system prompt and instruction discovery, agent tool data collection, tool runtime response poisoning, and poisoned model, dataset and agent-tool publication.

Separately, two existing detections gain additional technique tags, for multimodal prompt-injection triggers and for misconfigured or publicly exposed AI services. These are more precise labels on rules that already shipped, not new detections.

Detection accuracy and severity

  • Every ATLAS rule and the SBOM Drift Monitor now set alert.severity as an integer. String values were being coerced by Splunk and read back as 0, so triggered-alert severity in Splunk and any alert action keyed on it were unusable. Emitted severity fields, lookups and dashboard behaviour are unchanged.
  • A severity rubric pass re-rated three rules added in the previous release and confirmed nine others.
  • Five MITRE ATLAS technique names and tactics were corrected to the catalog text, and coverage is now scoped against ATLAS 2026.09 with a recorded disposition for every technique added in that catalog release.
  • Three regression guards now run before every package build: one validates every technique stamp against the shipped lookup, including secondary stamps; one validates the severity mapping on every rule; and one verifies that shared facts agree across the README, the deployment guide and the shipped artifacts.

Compliance citation corrections

No assessment logic changed. Citations and control identifiers were corrected across seven of the nine frameworks SCIP assesses:

  • EU Cyber Resilience Act control IDs now use the regulation's own Annex and Article labels; two transposed points corrected; coverage added for two security-update provisions. Now 21 controls.
  • FDA 524B: transposed statutory citations corrected, the patch-cycle control re-cited, the cyber device definition restored to its three statutory prongs, and guidance-derived rows distinguished from statutory ones. Now 21 controls.
  • NIST CSF 2.0: 16 subcategory descriptions replaced with CSF 2.0 outcome text.
  • PCI DSS 4.0.1 and FedRAMP: requirement and control titles restored to official text.
  • HIPAA: four rows re-titled to the standard's own name; a control that was being assessed twice is now out of scope.
  • DORA: incident classification and ICT concentration risk re-cited.
  • A nightly cleanup now retires status records for controls that are no longer in scope, so renamed or descoped controls leave nothing frozen behind.
  • Compliance views and the CSV export now carry a Last Assessed column, flagging any status older than two days as stale.

Functional fixes

  • The POA&M population search collided its inline time bounds with its dispatch window and scanned nothing while reporting success.
  • Five scheduled searches stored a search string beginning with a literal search command, which silently excluded events whose raw text lacked that word.
  • Setup, Remediation Tracking and Telemetry Settings could write to the KV Store on page load, before any Save action. All three now write only on an explicit action.
  • Telemetry Settings rewrote the license collection on every page view; it now updates a single record on an explicit selection.
  • The license status check treated a record with a missing or non-numeric expiry as active.
  • Risk score pruning deleted rows with a missing or non-numeric timestamp; those rows are now retained.
  • Incomplete SBOM baseline rows no longer suppress the set-a-baseline prompts or count toward baselined-application totals.

Setup and onboarding

  • The Setup page now names every index SCIP requires, states that SCIP does not create them, gives both standalone and clustered paths, and warns when any is missing.
  • A new section explains that SBOM drift's component, version and count signals are inactive until a baseline is set.
  • The file monitor section states that both SBOM inputs ship disabled, that the monitored path must be repointed, and that SPDX files belong in their own directory.
  • NVD API key copy corrected in four places.
  • The license blocklist field no longer shows an internal placeholder on load, and the blocklist is emptied through an explicit Clear action.

Air-gapped and egress-restricted deployments

CISA KEV and EPSS threat intelligence can now be refreshed by file transfer, as NVD and OSV already could. Both feeds write normalized records to spool directories that new file-monitor inputs index. Previously both were script-only, so without outbound access they stayed frozen at install, silently degrading KEV-driven risk scoring. The IL Deployment Guide documents the record formats and procedure.

Roles and user experience

All three SCIP roles gain eleven read and UI capabilities that restore the Apps menu icons and the Setup credential-status read. The administrative role retains the capabilities its credential-save controls require.

Documentation

New ATLAS coverage manifest and a guide to authoring your own ATLAS detections on top of the shipped baseline. The deployment guide now lists every required index in both its standalone and clustered instructions, documents scheduled searches that ship disabled by design, and corrects the outbound-connection table, which described telemetry as opt-out. Telemetry is opt-in and off by default.

Upgrade notes

  • Role assignment. SCIP roles are additive. If a user was assigned a SCIP role as their only role, they have been without the top-right username and account menu since v1.1.11. Assign your organization's base Splunk role alongside the SCIP role.
  • Saved-search renames. EU CRA and FDA compliance saved searches were renamed to match their new control identifiers. Any local override or external reference to the old stanza names must be updated.
  • Alert severity. Triggered-alert severity now reports real values instead of 0. Alert actions keyed on severity will begin seeing 2 through 5.
  • HIPAA control count drops from 9 to 8 in-scope controls. The descoped control's saved search is disabled rather than deleted, preserving the audit trail.


Short Description:
Unifies software supply chain risk (SBOM/SCA), MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detection, and nine-framework compliance in one Splunk app — with FedRAMP-ready audit exports and no external security product required.


Description:
SCIP unifies software composition analysis (SCA), supply chain risk monitoring, and AI threat detection in one Splunk app. Ingest SBOMs, correlate components against live vulnerability intelligence (OSV, NVD, CISA KEV, EPSS), detect adversarial AI/ML threats with MITRE ATLAS, and assess compliance posture across nine global frameworks — with detection logic written as transparent SPL you can open and read, and no external security product required. CAPABILITIES - SBOM ingestion — file-drop or HEC, supporting CycloneDX (JSON/XML) and SPDX (JSON) - Vulnerability correlation — daily OSV feed (264,944+ records across 11 ecosystems) with PURL-based correlation; NVD CPE-based correlation; CISA KEV matching; EPSS exploit-probability scoring - Air-gapped operation — all four intelligence feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA KEV, EPSS) refresh by file transfer, with no outbound connectivity required - Supply Chain Risk Score — 0–100 global and per-application risk scoring weighted by severity, KEV status, and EPSS - Vendor Risk — per-vendor risk aggregation and letter-grading across your SBOM portfolio - SBOM Drift Detection — baseline-vs-current component change tracking - License Compliance — GPL/AGPL/copyleft detection and license-risk classification - MITRE ATLAS Detection — 81 AI/agentic threat detection rules (72 mapped to 57 MITRE ATLAS techniques) - Silent-Source Detection — alerts when an enrolled AI/LLM telemetry source goes quiet, so a dead pipe is never mistaken for a clean one - Compliance Gap Assessment — nine frameworks: PCI DSS 4.0.1, NIST CSF 2.0, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA Security Rule, EU Cyber Resilience Act, FedRAMP / RMF / CISA, DORA, FDA 524B Premarket Cybersecurity, SEBI CSCRF - Long-Unpatched Critical Exposure — flags critical/high-severity vulnerabilities unpatched 180+ days - POA&M & FedRAMP Workflow — POA&M dashboard, monthly ConMon package builder, BOD 26-04 risk-tier classification (CISA's four-variable model with computed deadlines), deviation request workflow. Dashboards always available; automated POA&M generation is opt-in from Setup - Coverage-Evidence Manifest — AU-12-aligned attestation of unbroken AI-monitoring coverage - Audit-ready exports — FedRAMP POA&M Workbook (R3.0 and R2.1), SSP Appendix M Integrated Inventory, Deviation Request Form (Template 2.1 / Aug 2024) - Component Search — instant cross-SBOM component lookup - Compound Risk — correlates active MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detections with KEV-listed or critical-severity vulnerabilities on the same application, surfacing compounding risk neither signal shows alone - AI/ML Bill of Materials — catalogs AI/ML model components from your SBOMs (architecture, training data, lineage) with insecure-serialization-format flagging and risk classification SUPPORT GIC Engineering Consultants — contact@gicengineeringconsultants.com

Description:
Splunk AI Assistant is your AI-powered Agentic companion for getting answers from your data in Splunk. Whether you're a seasoned expert or just starting out, it helps you discover, analyze, and act on your data through natural conversation — going far beyond writing and explaining SPL. https://youtu.be/ynRBiepXVw4?si=eua38GwP0nwuvk3m With Agent Mode, the assistant reasons through your requests, takes actions on your behalf, and leverages a growing set of tools and skills from a single chat window. It decomposes complex questions into parallel steps, exposes its reasoning to build trust, and asks clarifying questions when prompts are ambiguous. What it can do for you: 🚀 SPL Generation, Editing & Optimization: Describe your search in plain English and get accurate SPL — or modify existing queries without rewriting, while making them faster. 📖 SPL Explanation: Understand any search in plain English, with a detailed breakdown of its logic. 🔍 Data Discovery: Don't know where your data lives? The assistant scans your environment to find the right sources. ⚡ Search Execution & Analysis: With your permission, it runs searches and summarizes results in chat — so you get answers, not just queries. 📊 Content Discovery: Semantically search across dashboards, saved searches, reports, and lookups — the assistant finds and reuses the best-matching content through natural language. 📚 Knowledge Retrieval: Get answers about Splunk documentation, platform terms, and products. 🎯 ITSI Integration (Read-Only): Bring IT Service Intelligence into the conversation — retrieve service health, KPIs, episodes, and related insights without leaving chat. 🌐 SPL2 & Federated Search (Beta): The assistant now supports SPL2 and Federated Search, including the Machine Data Lake, so you can query data across multiple sources and tiers. 🧰 More Tools in Agent Mode: This release expands Agent Mode with additional tools and skills, so the assistant can handle more of your workflows end to end. Teach AI (Beta): Admins can provide custom instructions via a markdown file to teach the assistant their org's best practices, data catalog, and guardrails — for smarter, more relevant results. Context Settings: Formerly Personalization, this generates more contextual results using non-personal metadata while honoring role-based access controls. Admins have full visibility into data collected. Model Runtime Choices: The assistant leverages Azure OpenAI models alongside Splunk-hosted LLMs for the best response quality. Availability: Splunk Cloud customers in AWS and Azure commercial regions, FedRAMP IL2, and Enterprise customers via Cloud Connected. Agent Mode is available to AWS commercial Splunk Cloud customers with this release. (c) Splunk 2026. All rights reserved.

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Version 1.0.52 improves the reliability, security, and usability of Insights Workspaces, topology maps, Searchbase searches, Dashboard Studio dashboards, and Guided Setup. ### Highlights * Expanded reusable Cisco searches across Catalyst Center, ISE, ThousandEyes, Cisco Spaces, Secure Firewall, data center, and security operations. * Added Secure Networking Pillars with five investigation areas and 30 Searchbase-powered cards. * Rebuilt the in-app User Guide with clearer workspace creation, sharing, permissions, persistence, Signal Rail, and topology instructions. * Improved light and dark theme readability throughout workspace editors, drawers, map controls, setup pages, and dashboards. ### Topology and ThousandEyes * Fixed topology-map creation and first-save failures. * Prevented stale editor tabs from overwriting newer shared topology changes. * Added protection against malformed or incomplete stored topology configurations. * Fixed Searchbase-bound link telemetry remaining in a loading state while the same search worked from Open in Search. * Improved ThousandEyes agent-to-agent selection so tests are discovered from the deployment’s observed data instead of relying on a hard-coded test ID. * Added safer confirmation flows for discarding drafts and restoring factory topology. * Improved map controls, attribution, keyboard access, and editing permissions. ### Search and dashboard reliability * Corrected dotted-field aggregation across Cisco Spaces, Catalyst Center, Meraki, and reusable Searchbase searches. * Fixed Catalyst Center multivalue health fields and prevented unavailable `-1` scores from appearing as 0% health. * Updated health tiles to show the latest valid score with its reporting age. * Fixed operational searches, adaptive time buckets, forecast confidence bands, anomaly fields, and data-model acceleration behavior. * Replaced the resource-intensive Threat Sources calculation with an accelerated Network Traffic data-model search while retaining Cisco firewall filtering. * Improved Guided Setup discovery, progress reporting, cancellation, retries, CIM allowlist detection, and macro persistence. ### Security and compatibility * Updated shipped JavaScript dependencies, including a critical MapLibre GL JS cross-site scripting fix. * Retained React 18.3.1 compatibility with the supported Splunk UI dependency line. * Restricted shared workspace, topology, and background-image administration to authorized roles. * Removed customer-identifying and deployment-specific content from the shipped catalogue. * Strengthened release packaging to exclude development-only and local-secret resources. ### Upgrade action Topology link bindings are stored by search display name. If a link used the former customer-specific ThousandEyes agent-to-agent search, open the map editor and rebind it to: `Overview - Link ThousandEyes A2A Health` Also reselect any affected NetOps Readiness or Cisco Spaces searches whose display names changed from “exercise” terminology to “surge event.” Search stanza IDs did not change, so dashboards, drilldowns, and saved searches that reference stanza IDs are unaffected.


Short Description:
Configurable executive, IT operations, and secure networking dashboards unifying Cisco network health, identity, security, infrastructure, application, and topology data in Splunk.


Description:
Beta release: Participation is by invitation only and limited to a small group of approved users. The app is not yet publicly downloadable on Splunkbase, and access requests are not currently being accepted. General availability is targeted for fall 2026. Splunk App for Secure Networking helps organizations turn fragmented Cisco infrastructure, networking, identity, security, application experience, and building telemetry into clear executive and operational insights in Splunk. Cisco environments often produce data across multiple products, add-ons, indexes, sourcetypes, and data models. item.title: Add-on for Prisma Cloud Audit - v2.0.1 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
### Fixed * **Infinite loop / stuck input process.** Every failure path (auth call fails, no token in auth response, data call fails, empty result page) previously logged an error and looped back immediately with no exit condition — the modular input would spin forever, re-hitting the Prisma Cloud API with no backoff, and never exit. All paths now terminate the run. * **Unhandled crash on non-JSON error bodies (`JSONDecodeError`).** `response.json()` / `auth_response.json()` were called inline inside `.format()` calls with no error handling. A 5xx response with an empty or non-JSON body raised an uncaught `JSONDecodeError`, killing the script with a raw traceback instead of a clean log line. Both the auth response and the data response JSON parsing are now wrapped in `try/except ValueError`, logging the raw response text and exiting cleanly. * **Silent error messages.** `"error in data collection".format(response.json())` and similar calls had no `{}` placeholder, so the parsed response body was discarded — errors logged with zero detail. Now logs the actual response body (`response.text` / `auth_response.text`). * **Misleading exit-condition log message.** The message logged when there's nothing new to collect said `"end_date>start_date.existing the script!"`, which was backwards (it fires when `start_date >= end_date`) and had a typo. Corrected to `"start_date>=end_date, nothing new to collect. exiting the script!"`. * **Empty-page handling.** A data response with no `value` records previously skipped the entire pagination/checkpoint block, leaving `keep_running` untouched — another path into the infinite loop. Now logs, saves a checkpoint, and exits cleanly. ### Changed * Genuine failures (auth failure, missing token, data-fetch HTTP error, malformed JSON, checkpoint-save exception) now `raise RuntimeError(...)` instead of just logging. This surfaces failed runs to the `splunktaucclib` framework (which logs the traceback and marks the run as failed) instead of exiting silently as if successful — important for noticing things like bad credentials or persistent API errors. * Benign "nothing to do" cases (no new time range, no records this cycle) still exit cleanly without raising, since they aren't errors. ### Removed * Dead code: an unused `headers` dict (apikey-style auth header) that was built but never passed to any request — the actual calls use `auth_headers` / `data_headers`. ### Verified * `python3 -m py_compile` passes with no syntax errors. * Confirmed against a live 500-error and JSON-decode-error traceback, and a live invalid-credentials scenario — both now produce a single clean `RuntimeError` with the real API error message instead of a raw crash or silent infinite retry. ###

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**# TA-Vulnerability catalog 1.1.0 — Release notes** Released: 2026-09-19 Previous version: 1.0.0 **---** **## New features** **\*\*CISA Vulnrichment data input\*\*** A third data source has been added: the CISA Vulnrichment repository (\`cisagov/vulnrichment\`), indexed under the new sourcetype \`vulninfo:vulnrichment\`. \* The first run streams the branch tarball and indexes every record, without consuming the   GitHub API rate limit. Subsequent runs walk the GitHub Commits API from the last processed   commit SHA and index only the CVE files that were added or changed. \* Events retain the **\*\*complete raw CVE Record 5.x JSON\*\***, with CIM fields extracted in front   of it — nothing from the source record is discarded. \* CISA ADP enrichment is exposed as searchable fields: SSVC decision points   (\`ssvc\_exploitation\`, \`ssvc\_automatable\`, \`ssvc\_technical\_impact\`), KEV membership   (\`is\_known\_exploited\`, \`kev\_date\_added\`), CVSS vectors and CWE identifiers. \* Mapped to the CIM **\*\*Vulnerabilities\*\*** data model: \`cve\`, \`signature\`, \`cvss\`, \`severity\`,   \`severity\_id\`, \`cwe\`, \`category\`, \`vendor\_product\`, \`url\`, \`xref\`, \`vuln\_published\_time\`,   \`vuln\_modified\_time\`, \`dest\`, \`dvc\`. \* A GitHub personal access token can optionally be configured to raise the API rate limit   from 60 to 5,000 requests per hour. No token scopes are required. \* \`Seed max files\` allows the initial full load to be split across several runs, resuming   from the same pinned commit snapshot. **\*\*Full reload option on every input\*\*** All three inputs now have a \`Full reload\` checkbox. When enabled, the input ignores its checkpoint and re-ingests the entire dataset on the next run — useful after changing the destination index or losing indexed data. A warning is logged on every run while it is on, as a reminder to turn it back off. **\*\*Expanded CIM coverage for the KEV catalog\*\*** \`vulninfo:kevcatalog\` now populates \`dest\`, \`dvc\` and \`severity\_id\`, which were previously absent. KEV rows in the Vulnerabilities data model are no longer missing \`dest\`. **---** **## Fixes** **\*\*Checkpoints are now scoped per input instance\*\*** The KEV and EPSS inputs previously stored their progress under a fixed checkpoint key, shared by every instance of that input. As a result, running two instances of the same input caused them to overwrite each other's progress, and deleting and recreating an input under a different name did not start from a clean state. Checkpoint keys now include the input instance name (\`kev\_catalog\_state\_v2\_\\`, \`epss\_last\_score\_date\_\\`), so instances are fully independent. **\*\*Upgrading does not cause re-ingestion:\*\*** on the first run after upgrade, each input adopts the value from its old key and logs the migration. **\*\*EPSS no longer risks repeated full re-ingestion\*\*** The EPSS input used the snapshot's \`score\_date\` — read from the CSV header comment — as its checkpoint, and skipped saving the checkpoint entirely when that value could not be parsed. If the upstream header format ever changed, the checkpoint would never advance and the full snapshot (300,000+ events) would be re-indexed on every interval, duplicating indefinitely. The checkpoint is now always saved. When \`score\_date\` is unavailable, a hash of the snapshot content is used instead, and a warning is logged. Collection continues normally and unchanged snapshots are still skipped. **\*\*EPSS events removed from the CIM Vulnerabilities data model\*\*** \`vulninfo:epss\` carried a custom \`epss\` tag that matched no data model, which produced a warning in the add-on's data model mapping and placed the events in no dataset. EPSS scores are per-CVE probabilities rather than vulnerability records, so the mapping has been removed rather than completed. EPSS events remain fully searchable and are intended to be joined to the other sourcetypes on \`cve\`. **---** **## Upgrade notes** \* **\*\*Restart Splunk after upgrading.\*\*** The add-on adds a new modular input and new input   parameters; splunkd must re-read \`inputs.conf.spec\` before they take effect. \* **\*\*No re-ingestion occurs for existing inputs.\*\*** Legacy checkpoints migrate automatically on   the first run. The migration is logged:   \`index\=\_internal source\=\*ta\_vulnerability\_catalog\* "checkpoint migrated"\` \* **\*\*Before enabling the Vulnrichment input, check your license headroom.\*\*** The initial load   is 130,000–200,000 events at several KB to tens of KB each. \* **\*\*If you built searches on \`tag\=epss\`\*\***, switch them to \`sourcetype\=vulninfo:epss\`. The   eventtype and tag no longer exist. \* Each input must be enabled on exactly one node. Checkpoints are stored per node, so running   the same input on several nodes produces duplicate events. \------------------------------8\< note in Japanese------------------------------ **# TA-Vulnerability catalog 1.1.0 — リリースノート** リリース日: 2026-09-19 前バージョン: 1.0.0 **---** **## 新機能** **\*\*CISA Vulnrichment データ入力\*\*** 3つ目のデータソースとして CISA Vulnrichment リポジトリ（\`cisagov/vulnrichment\`）の取り込みに対応しました。新しい sourcetype \`vulninfo:vulnrichment\` でインデックスされます。 \* 初回はブランチの tarball をストリーミング展開して全件を取り込みます。GitHub API のレート制限を消費しません。2回目以降は、最後に処理したコミット SHA を起点にGitHub Commits API を辿り、追加・変更された CVE ファイルだけを取り込みます。 \* イベントは **\*\*CVE Record 5.x の生 JSON 全体をそのまま保持\*\***し、その手前に CIM フィールドを展開しています。元レコードの情報は一切欠落しません。 \* CISA ADP による拡充情報を検索可能なフィールドとして提供します。SSVC の判断項目   （\`ssvc\_exploitation\` / \`ssvc\_automatable\` / \`ssvc\_technical\_impact\`）、KEV 掲載有無   （\`is\_known\_exploited\` / \`kev\_date\_added\`）、CVSS ベクタ、CWE 識別子。 \* CIM **\*\*Vulnerabilities\*\*** データモデルにマッピング済みです。\`cve\` / \`signature\` / \`cvss\` /   \`severity\` / \`severity\_id\` / \`cwe\` / \`category\` / \`vendor\_product\` / \`url\` / \`xref\` /   \`vuln\_published\_time\` / \`vuln\_modified\_time\` / \`dest\` / \`dvc\`。 \* GitHub Personal Access Token を任意で設定でき、API のレート制限が 60 → 5,000リクエスト/時に上がります。トークンのスコープ（権限）は不要です。 \* \`Seed max files\` により、初回の全件取り込みを複数回の実行に分割できます。コミット SHA を固定したスナップショットから再開するため、分割しても取りこぼしは発生しません。 **\*\*全入力への Full reload オプション\*\*** 3つの入力すべてに \`Full reload\` チェックボックスを追加しました。有効にすると、次回の実行でチェックポイントを無視して全件を取り込み直します。取り込み先インデックスを変更した場合や、インデックス済みデータを失った場合に使用します。有効な間は実行のたびに警告ログを出力し、戻し忘れを防ぎます。 **\*\*KEV カタログの CIM フィールド拡充\*\*** \`vulninfo:kevcatalog\` が \`dest\` / \`dvc\` / \`severity\_id\` を出力するようになりました。従来はこれらが欠けており、Vulnerabilities データモデル上で KEV の行だけ \`dest\` が空になっていました。 **---** **## 修正ポイント** **\*\*チェックポイントを入力インスタンス単位に分離\*\*** KEV と EPSS の入力は、取り込み位置を**\*\*固定のキー\*\***に保存していました。このキーは同じ入力の全インスタンスで共有されるため、同一入力を2つ作ると互いの進捗を上書きし合い、また入力を削除して別名で作り直しても初期状態から始まりませんでした。 チェックポイントのキーに入力インスタンス名を含めるよう変更し\`kev\_catalog\_state\_v2\_\<入力名>\` / \`epss\_last\_score\_date\_\<入力名>\`）、インスタンスが完全に独立して動作するようになりました。**\*\*アップグレードによる再取り込みは発生しません。\*\*** アップグレード後の初回実行時に旧キーの値を自動で引き継ぎ、移行をログに記録します。 **\*\*EPSS の全件再取り込みループを防止\*\*** EPSS 入力は、CSV のヘッダーコメントから読み取ったスナップショットの \`score\_date\` をチェックポイントとしていましたが、この値が取得できない場合はチェックポイントを**\*\*一切保存しない\*\***実装になっていました。配布元のヘッダー書式が変わると、チェックポイントが永久に更新されず、実行間隔ごとに全件（30万件以上）を再インデックスし続け、重複が際限なく増える状態に陥ります。 チェックポイントを必ず保存するよう修正しました。\`score\_date\` が取得できない場合はスナップショット本文のハッシュを代替キーとして使用し、警告ログを出力します。取り込みは継続され、内容が変わらないスナップショットは従来どおりスキップされます。 **\*\*EPSS イベントを CIM Vulnerabilities データモデルから除外\*\*** **New: real-time vulnerability lifecycle tracking** This release adds a new input, Sysdig Vulnerability Findings, alongside the existing one. Instead of re-sending your entire vulnerability snapshot on every poll, it tracks each vulnerability's lifecycle and sends only what changed: opened, updated, or fixed. Benefits: * Dramatically fewer and smaller events, since unchanged findings are no longer re-sent every cycle. * Accurate event timestamps reflecting when a vulnerability was actually detected or fixed, not just when the input happened to run. * Correctly groups vulnerabilities across all workload types, including Kubernetes, AWS Lambda, ECS, Cloud Run, Azure Container services, and containers running directly on hosts, so a workload's vulnerability history stays stable and doesn't flip between fixed and reopened without a real change. Note that workloads running multiple containers may report a few more findings than a single combined one would, since each container is tracked individually for an accurate "currently in use" status. * Faster, simpler searches: | tstats latest(state) by finding\_id | where state!\="fixed" * gives you current posture directly, instead of aggregating a full daily dump. The existing input keeps working exactly as before under its own sourcetype, so upgrading is non-breaking. You can run both side by side, or switch your dashboards to the new sourcetype (sysdig:secure:vulnerability\_findings) at your own pace. See the add-on's documentation for setup and example searches. **Fixed: Splunk Cloud compatibility** The add-on has been rebuilt on the current Splunk UCC framework, resolving a Splunk Cloud Platform compatibility issue flagged by Splunk on the previous release. **Compatibility** Supports Python 3.9 and 3.13 (Splunk Enterprise 9.4–10.5).

Product(s) Enabled: Cisco AI Defense Cisco Duo Cisco Email Threat Defense (ETD) Cisco Endpoint Visibility Module (EVM) CIM Mappings (Beta) Cisco Identity Intelligence (CII) Cisco Multicloud Defense Cisco NVM Cisco Secure Endpoint Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD/eStreamer/ASA) Cisco Secure Workload Cisco Isovalent Cisco Isovalent Edge Processor **Alpha Cisco Secure Malware Analytics (SMA) Cisco Secure Network Analytics (SNA) Cisco Vulnerability Intelligence Cisco XDR (Incident Import & Promote to ES Notable) Here’s the revised version with the sourcetype list and stronger 3.x transition language. **MAJOR VERSION CHANGE: CiscoSecurityCloud 4.0.0 Release Notes** CiscoSecurityCloud 4.0.0 introduces expanded Cisco Secure Firewall / FTD syslog and Advanced Logging support, with improved parsing, event routing, CIM/data model alignment, dashboard visibility, and ingestion reliability. This release adds a new FTD sourcetype routing model that separates FTD events by event family instead of keeping all events under a single generic `cisco:ftd:syslog` sourcetype. This improves field extraction accuracy, dashboard filtering, data model mapping, and long-term supportability for FTD syslog and Advanced Logging data. Because this changes how FTD events are categorized, **4.0.0 may be a breaking change for customers with custom Splunk content**. Content that may require review includes: - Saved searches, alerts, reports, and dashboards that filter only on `sourcetype="cisco:ftd:syslog"` - Custom macros, eventtypes, tags, and CIM/data model constraints - Custom props/transforms or routing assumptions for FTD syslog - Data model acceleration searches scoped to the previous FTD sourcetype - External integrations or correlation searches that expect all FTD events in one sourcetype Customers should update broad FTD searches from "cisco:ftd:syslog" to cisco:ftd:intrusion cisco:ftd:connection cisco:ftd:connection:security cisco:ftd:file cisco:ftd:malware cisco:ftd:discovery cisco:ftd:useractivity cisco:ftd:correlation cisco:ftd:intrusionpacket cisco:ftd:adv:http cisco:ftd:adv:ftp cisco:ftd:adv:conn cisco:ftd:adv:dns cisco:ftd:adv:weird cisco:ftd:adv:notice CiscoSecurityCloud 4.0.0 is intended for customers who want the new FTD Advanced Logging model and are ready to validate custom content against the expanded sourcetypes. Description:
The Xage Fabric TA is a technical add-on that ingests and normalizes Xage Fabric syslog audit logs into Splunk's Common Information Model. The add-on parses RFC5424-formatted syslog messages containing JSON audit payloads, extracting authentication events, configuration changes, and security alerts. Events are automatically tagged and mapped to the CIM Authentication, Change, and Alerts data models. The add-on handles both TCP and UDP syslog inputs as well as file-based monitoring, and performs sourcetype classification at index time to ensure proper field extraction.
